name: Emergency Preparedness Checklist
description: A complete household readiness checklist covering your plan, supplies, documents, communication and special needs.

items.text: Sign up for local emergency alerts and warnings
Choose two meeting places: one near home and one outside the neighborhood
Pick an out-of-town contact everyone can call or text
items.note: Texts often go through when calls fail during an emergency

items.text: Map at least two evacuation routes out of your area
Plan how to reunite with children at school or daycare
Practice the plan with the whole family twice a year
Store one gallon of water per person per day for at least three days
Keep a three-day supply of non-perishable food per person
Include a manual can opener and basic eating utensils
Add food for infants, pets and anyone with special diets
Label storage dates and rotate stock before it expires
Stock a first aid kit and any prescription medications
Pack flashlights and a battery- or hand-crank radio
Keep extra batteries and a power bank for phones
Add a whistle to signal for help
Include dust masks, work gloves and plastic sheeting
Pack moist towelettes, garbage bags and ties for sanitation
Copy IDs, passports, birth and marriage certificates
Save insurance policies, deeds and lease agreements
List bank, medical and emergency contact information
Store copies in a waterproof bag and a secure cloud account
Keep some cash in small bills in case card systems are down
Save emergency contacts on every family member's phone
Write key numbers on a card in case phones die
Keep chargers, a power bank and a car charger ready
Agree on a check-in time and method if you are separated
items.note: A shared group text or messaging thread keeps everyone updated

items.text: Know how to receive alerts if the power and internet are out

sections.title: Plan for Special Needs and Pets

items.text: Pack a week of medications and copies of prescriptions
Include supplies for infants, seniors and disabilities
Store spare glasses, hearing-aid batteries and mobility aids
Prepare food, water, leash, carrier and vaccination records for pets
Identify pet-friendly shelters or hotels along evacuation routes
Add comfort items and activities for children

faq.q: How much water should I store for an emergency?
faq.a: Store at least one gallon of water per person per day for a minimum of three days — that covers drinking and basic sanitation. Keep more if you have children, pets, or live in a hot climate, and aim for a two-week supply at home when you can.

faq.q: How long should my emergency supplies last?
faq.a: Build at least a three-day (72-hour) supply for evacuation and aim for two weeks of supplies to shelter at home. Authorities such as Ready.gov and the Red Cross recommend the 72-hour minimum as a baseline for every household.

faq.q: What is the most important first step in emergency preparedness?
faq.a: Make a written family emergency plan. Decide how you will get alerts, where you will meet, how you will communicate if cell service is down, and your evacuation routes. A plan turns a kit into a coordinated response.

faq.q: How often should I update my emergency kit?
faq.a: Review your kit at least twice a year. Rotate food and water before they expire, refresh medications, replace dead batteries, and update documents and clothing sizes for growing children.

faq.q: Is this emergency preparedness checklist printable?
faq.a: Yes. Print it or download the PDF, keep a copy with your kit and one on the fridge, and tick off each task as your household gets ready.
